sentences.text: Present appeal has been filed by the injured-claimant seeking enhancement of compensation of Rs.9.62 lacs granted by Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Rohtak (hereinafter referred to as 'the Tribunal') vide Award dated 5.4.2016 passed in MACT Case No.81 of 8.4.2015 filed u/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').

Ld. Tribunal on the basis of pleadings and evidence on record held that the claimant/appellant suffered injuries in a motor vehicular accident that took place on 19.11.2013 due to rash and negligent driving of truck bearing registration No. HR-46-C-6106 (hereinafter referred to as 'the offending vehicle') being driven by respondent no.1, owned by respondent no.2 and insured by respondent no.3.
The Tribunal awarded compensation as above alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of filing of the claim petition till realization.
Liability to pay the compensation was joint and several.
FAO 5870/2016(O&M) 2023:PHHC:056005 Ld. counsel seeks enhancement of compensation on the ground that income of the appellant has been taken on lower side as only Rs.6600/- per month.

It is submitted that father of the appellant is owner of 9 acres of agriculture land and appellant used Ajit vs Bijender Singh And Ors on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65512479/
1 to help his father from which they were earning Rs.17,000/- per acre.

sentences.text: It is submitted that however,
ld . Tribunal
has discarded the evidence produced by the appellant and has taken the income of the appellant as only Rs.6600/- per month as admissible to an unskilled labourer.
It is submitted that income of the deceased ought to have been taken at least Rs.8337.10 as admissible to a skilled labourer.

It is then submitted that permanent disability certificate shows that the appellant has suffered 70%
permanent disability due to amputation of his right lower leg.
It is submitted that appellant is unable to walk properly what to talk of being able to do any work.
It is submitted that the appellant is using artificial foot, however nothing has been awarded by the Tribunal for future treatment or for amount spent on prosthetic.

It is submitted that the appellant was 20 years old at the time of accident and his whole life was before him yet, ld. Tribunal has assessed loss of income due to disability of the appellant to the extent of 50% only whereas, the same ought to have been taken as 100%.
It is further submitted that nothing has been granted towards future prospects, pain and suffering, loss of enjoyment of life, loss of amenities, marriage prospects etc.

In support, ld. counsel relies upon judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Anant son of Sidheshwar Dukre v Pratap son of Zhamnappa Lamzane and another, Law Finder Doc Id # 1141284; Syed Sadiq Etc. v Divisional Manager, United India Ins. Co., Law Finder Doc Id # 515167; and of this High FAO 5870/2016(O&M) 2023:PHHC:056005 Court in Dina Nath Dhiman v Jaswinder Singh and others,
Law Finder Doc Id # 749502.
Ld. counsel further relies upon judgment of this Court in Parveen v Vikram and others, Law Finder Doc Id # 752898, the relevant head note of which is also extracted below:-
Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, Sections 166 and 168 Computation of compensation in injury cases of 100% Permanent disability - Percentage of permanent disability is the relevant factor for applying multiplier to compute the loss of future income on account of loss of earning capacity - Claimant suffered 70% permanent disability which has to be take 100% functional disability - Age of claimant was 20 years at the time of accident- Multiplier of 18 has to be applied - 50% of his income added towards prospectuses of increase - Claimant held entitled to compensation under the heads of disability, actual medical expenses, loss of income, salary to attendant assuming life expectancy to be 55 years, special diet, pain and suffering loss of amenities and expectation of life and transportation and misc.
expenses etc and awarded Rs. 24,90,650/-.

In response, it is submitted by the ld. counsel for the respondent Insurance Company that no evidence was led by the appellant in support of his claim that his father was owner of 9 acres of land and that he had agriculture income of Rs.17000/- per month and accordingly,
income
of the appellant
has been correctly assessed as Rs.6600/- per month on the basis of relevant minimum wage notification as admissible to unskilled labourer.
It is very fairly admitted that appellant is entitled to addition of future FAO 5870/2016(O&M) 2023:PHHC:056005 prospects @ 40%.

However, no case law to Ajit vs Bijender Singh And Ors on 18 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65512479/
2 the contrary is cited by ld.
Counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company.

sentences.text: No other argument has been raised by the ld. counsel for the parties.
Heard ld. counsel.

Perusal of the impugned Award shows that ld. Tribunal has calculated the compensation payable to the appellant as follows:-
"15.
The petitioner in his statement has not stated his annual income.

PW5 Dharambir has stated that he has leased out nine acres of the land to Ajit Singh, the petitioner in the name of his father at the rate of Rs.17,000/- per acre, but no corroborative evidence has been placed on the record to show the extent of income earned by petitioner Ajit Singh from this land.
In these circumstances, the minimum wages prevalent in the year 2013 as Rs.6600/- per month is taken as the income of the injured 50% of the same income is assessed as loss of income and
as such it comes to Rs.3300/- per month and Rs.39,600/- per annum.
Since, the age of the injured is twenty years, the multiplier of 18 shall be applied and if the multiplier of 18 is applied, the loss of income comes to Rs.7,12,800/-.
Besides this, an amount of Rs.50,000/- is awarded on account of pain and suffering due to amputation of right leg and surgery of the petitioner.
The petitioner has also placed on record the medical bills of medicines and hospitalization the total of which comes to Rs.1,49,008/-.
Since, the right leg of the petitioner has been amputated his marriage prospectus have also been diminished.
As such, on this count, he is also awarded Rs.50,000/-.

T h u s , i n t o t a l , t h e a m o u n t c o m p e n s a t i o n F A O 5 8 7 0 / 2 0 1 6 ( O & M )
2023:PHHC:056005 comes to Rs.9,61,808/- say Rs.9,62,000/-.
Thus, issue No.2 is decided in favour of the petitioner".

In my view ld. Tribunal is in error in ignoring the testimony of PW5 Dharambir who has stated that he leased out 9 acres of land to the appellant in the name of his father @ Rs.17,000/- per acre,
clearly therefore, appellant used to help manage and till the said land, therefore, income of the appellant ought to have been taken as per minimum wages admissible to a skilled labourer.
In the present case, as per relevant Minimum Wage Notification, the same is Rs.8337.10 (rounded off to Rs.8400/-) per month w.e.f. 1.9.2014.
Further, ld. Tribunal has only granted 50% loss of income due to disability suffered by the appellant.
However, as per above cited case law, disability of the appellant is to be taken as 100% in view of the admitted fact that permanent disability of the appellant is 70%.
Accordingly, loss of income due to disability has to be taken as 100%.
Further addition of Rs.3360/- as 40% future prospects is also required to be made.

Accordingly, enhanced compensation payable to the appellant works out as under:-
